title: A City-funded charity’s own ballot-measure money
question: How much did a City-funded charity, Tenants and Owners Development Corporation (TODCO), report giving to San Francisco campaigns in its own name, and does that fit what its tax returns report as lobbying?
finding: TODCO, filing as a major donor together with its affiliate Yerba Buena Neighborhood Consortium, reported $2,448,204 in contributions and campaign payments from 2014 to 2024: $1,126,393 to committees it sponsors (Build Affordable Faster CA; Housing Forward SF) and $1,321,810 to other committees and campaign vendors. $62,329 went to political clubs’ committees with no measure named on the filing. The City paid TODCO $3,654,566 in fiscal 2019 to 2026. In the year to June 2024 its filings show $80,500 of campaign money against $51,000 of lobbying on its tax return; in the other years from 2021 the return’s figure is the larger.
how: Form 461 Part 5 rows filed by TODCO and its affiliate in the Ethics Commission’s campaign transactions, latest filing version, each date, amount and payee counted once; transfers between TODCO and the affiliate left out. Summed by TODCO’s tax year (July to June) and set beside Schedule C, Part II-A (total lobbying expenditures) of each Form 990 on disk. City payments: vendor TENANTS & OWNERS DEVELOPMENT CORP.
limits: A ballot-measure contribution by a charity is counted as lobbying on its return, not as campaign activity, so the comparison is of like with like; but a payment itemised under two measures appears twice in the filings, and the return may book a payment in another year. The filings are made jointly with the affiliate, and the records do not show which entity’s money paid each item; the returns list Yerba Buena Consortium LLC as a disregarded entity of TODCO. A club committee may have spent the money on measures. City grants carry their own use restrictions, and nothing here shows City money was used.
